title: Customer Insights - Data: MCP server grounds agents in unified customer profiles and insights
summary: Hold: the Microsoft Entra consent path starts inside an app registration without telling administrators how to reach that app. The roadmap facts, gateway commands, security behaviour and billing statements are supported; the registry and maker paths need small clarifications. All cited Learn pages opened successfully in this check.

claims.claim: The Customer Insights Model Context Protocol server exposes Customer Insights capabilities as tools for agents and chat clients.
claims.quote: The Customer Insights Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data and select Customer Insights - Journeys capabilities as callable tools for LLM agents.

claims.claim: An agent can resolve a Dataverse contact to its unified customer profile.
claims.quote: Resolves a unified customer ID from a Dataverse contact GUID.

claims.claim: An agent can resolve a Dataverse lead to its unified customer profile.
claims.quote: Resolves a unified customer ID from a record identifier in an ingested source system. ... Call list_data_sources first to find valid source entity names, such as contact, lead, or a custom table.

claims.claim: Agents can read a unified customer's Customer Insights - Data segment membership.
claims.quote: Lists the Customer Insights - Data segments or audiences a unified customer belongs to.

claims.claim: Agents can read calculated customer measures.
claims.quote: Returns calculated customer measures and KPIs, such as lifetime value, order counts, and engagement scores.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Agents can read predictions such as churn probability and customer lifetime value.
claims.quote: Returns machine learning predictions for a unified customer, such as churn probability, predicted lifetime value, propensity scores, and next-best-product suggestions.

claims.claim: Agents can read cluster membership, including households.
claims.quote: Returns cluster membership, such as a household, and other members

claims.claim: Unified customer profiles combine Dataverse records with external sources such as loyalty or contract data.
claims.quote: Customer Insights - Data matches the lead and contact records and creates a unified customer profile that combines Dynamics 365 data with external contract data.

claims.claim: Makers add the server from the agent's Tools page using Add a tool, the MCP filter and a search for Dynamics 365 CX Customer Insights.
claims.quote: Go to the Tools page for your agent, and then select Add a tool. ... Select the MCP filter. ... Search for Dynamics 365 CX Customer Insights.

claims.claim: Learn documents external connections through the gateway for Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT and Claude Code.
claims.quote: Connect supported external MCP clients, such as Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Claude Code

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Tools requiring Customer Insights - Data are read-only.
claims.quote: create_journey is the only tool that writes data. ... Every other tool only reads.

claims.claim: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys.
claims.quote: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys, but each tool works with a specific app.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: create_journey writes data.
claims.quote: | create_journey | Create Journey | Validates, enriches, and creates a journey | Customer Insights - Journeys | No |

claims.claim: Customer profile tools read Dataverse virtual entities reflecting live unified customer data.
claims.quote: They read from Dataverse virtual entities, which reflect the live unified customer data that Customer Insights - Data creates, including its segments, measures, predictions, and clusters.

claims.claim: get_customer_details returns source records and personal profile attributes.
claims.quote: Core profile attributes, such as name, email, and address, with system columns excluded ... Source records that show data unification provenance

claims.claim: The returned source records identify which source supplied the winning value for each unified field.
claims.quote: Each source record includes ... a flag that identifies which source contributed the winning value for each unified field.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that Dynamics 365 connections to other services allow data to leave the Dynamics 365 FedRAMP High boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling connections between Dynamics 365 and non-Dynamics 365 services, including Microsoft or external services, allows data to leave the Dynamics 365 FedRAMP High boundary.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft asks the tenant administrator to confirm security, compliance, residency and governance requirements before enabling MCP connections.
claims.quote: Before you enable MCP server connections for your organization, your tenant administrator should confirm that these connections meet your data security, compliance, residency, and governance requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tools run in the calling user's context.
claims.quote: Authorization is enforced inside the tool logic using the caller's user context.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The server enforces row-level security.
claims.quote: Row-level security makes sure users only reach data they're authorized to see

claims.claim: Each tool checks privileges for the relevant entities.
claims.quote: Each tool checks entity-specific privileges, such as read access to consent purposes

claims.claim: The server never implicitly escalates privileges.
claims.quote: The MCP server never escalates privileges implicitly. Tools act as facades and never do anything beyond what the calling user is permitted to do.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Change & support
claims.claim: Tools can be missing from an agent when the calling user lacks privileges on the underlying Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: | Tools are missing from the agent | The calling user lacks privileges for the underlying Dataverse tables | Check the user's security role privileges. |

claims.claim: Connections use OAuth through Agent 365 Tooling Gateway.
claims.quote: Agent 365 Tooling Gateway is an OAuth 2.0-protected resource. ... The MCP client requests a token for the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway resource.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Using the /.default scope requires admin consent in advance.
claims.quote: The /.default scope doesn't support incremental or dynamic user consent, so admin consent must be granted in advance in the customer tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can consent to the named McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All delegated permission if the tenant permits user consent.
claims.quote: McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All is user-consentable. If your client requests that named permission instead of /.default, each person can consent for themselves ... as long as your tenant allows user consent for apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: External clients sign in with their own Microsoft Entra client apps, which need permission to call the gateway.
claims.quote: Each of these clients signs in with its own Microsoft Entra client app, so a tenant admin still needs to allow that client to call the gateway.

claims.claim: Each environment needs its own connector configuration because the server URL is environment-specific.
claims.quote: The server URL is specific to the environment, so each environment needs its own connector configuration.

claims.claim: A server URL missing /mcp/environments/ produces a 404 error.
claims.quote: The /mcp/environments/ path segment is required. If you leave it out, the request returns 404 RouteNotFound.

claims.claim: Using a tenant ID instead of the environment ID in the server URL produces a 400 error.
claims.quote: | 400 EndpointInvalid, with the message Environment id ... is invalid. | The /environments/ segment holds a tenant ID or a malformed GUID |

claims.claim: create_journey is not idempotent and retries can create duplicate journeys.
claims.quote: It isn't idempotent, so retrying a failed call can create a duplicate journey. Have your agent confirm the outcome before it retries.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Customer Insights is licensed per tenant.
claims.quote: Customer Insights is licensed per tenant and includes multiple capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Additional Customer Insights capacity can be purchased with add-on licences.
claims.quote: Customer Insights - Data is licensed per tenant. You can purchase more capacity with add-on licenses.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-insights/data/overview to sources for the explicit add-on capacity wording.

claims.claim: The feature's introductory page lists access to Dataverse tables as its sole prerequisite and names no MCP-server licence.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: The user must have access to the Dataverse tables.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Studio measures agent usage in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.

claims.claim: Employee-facing Copilot Studio agents and invoked tools are included in Microsoft Copilot USL when the user is licensed and the agent uses that authenticated identity.
claims.quote: Employee-facing usage scenarios (Business to Employee) of Copilot Studio agents and Copilot Studio tools and features that these agents invoke are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL ... Usage is limited to fair usage limits.
claims.fix: Append 'Usage is limited to fair usage limits.' to the sentence describing Microsoft Copilot USL inclusion, as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management.

claims.claim: The billing page states that agents incur charges for generative answer responses outside its listed exception.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.claim: The Billing rates and management page describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges Copilot Credits for tools including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: What is not published; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate MCP-server charge is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Insights Data MCP server separate licensing pricing charge per call add-on capacity. Read tools, tools reference, gateway, paid-license, overview and both Copilot Studio billing pages; no server-specific licence or rate found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect cost; Scope
claims.claim: Profile lookups need unified Customer Insights - Data profiles.
claims.quote: If you use only Customer Insights - Journeys, there are no unified customer profiles for these tools to read.

claims.claim: Consent, journey and email tools do not need a unified customer ID.
claims.quote: The consent, journey, and email tools don't need a unified customer ID.

claims.claim: Configuring the MCP server requires the System Administrator role.
claims.quote: The System Administrator role, to configure the MCP server

claims.claim: Manual or external-client setup requires tenant admin or delegated admin-consent permissions.
claims.quote: Tenant admin or delegated admin-consent permissions, to set up the server manually or to connect an external MCP client

claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in because gateway provisioning requires tenant-admin action before clients can obtain tokens.
claims.quote: Before a client app can request a token for it, the gateway service principal must exist in the customer tenant. As a tenant admin, run one of the following commands.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining the Customer Insights tenant licence and metered Copilot Studio usage.
claims.quote: When you purchase a Copilot Studio license, you get a specific number of billed Copilot Credits. You pool this capacity across the entire tenant.

claims.claim: Variable cost reflects the published Copilot Credits usage meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The tenant registry control is reached at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Agents > Tools > Registry. ... Select actions directly from the list, or select a tool to view its overview page.
claims.fix: For the availability control, extend controls[0].ui.path and its table path to 'Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block' and retain the note that Unblock restores access. The existing cited overview page documents selecting a tool and the Block action.

claims.claim: No API operation for the registered Customer Insights MCP server's tenant registry Block or Unblock control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Agent 365 Tools Registry block unblock MCP server API automation; Microsoft 365 Agent 365 tools registry MCP server block unblock Microsoft Graph API endpoint. Read registry overview and Manage plugins, skills, and MCP servers; no applicable operation found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Registry Block and Unblock govern supported experiences, not necessarily every product or connected component.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 provides administrative controls for supported tools. Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: The maker's per-agent selection control is Tools > select the MCP server > Allow all.
claims.quote: Go to the Tools tab for your agent. Select the MCP server from the list of tools. ... Tools: A list of names and descriptions for the MCP tools that the server offers. ... Turn off the Allow all toggle.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Tools > select the MCP server > Tools > Allow all' to include the settings page's Tools section. Qualify the row note with 'For agents powered by the standard harness', as the cited page does.

claims.claim: Turning off Allow all exposes individual tool toggles.
claims.quote: Turn off the Allow all toggle. Toggles become available for each of the individual tools.

claims.claim: Makers save and publish changes to make added or removed tools available to the agent.
claims.quote: Select Save. To make newly added or removed tools available to the agent, select Publish.

claims.claim: With Allow all off, new tools added to the server are off by default.
claims.quote: When you turn off Allow all, any new tools added to the MCP server are turned off by default.

claims.claim: The documented Copilot Studio tool toggles are maker-side controls for an individual agent.
claims.quote: If you don't want to use all the tools offered by an MCP server, you can selectively turn off MCP server tools directly in your agent.

claims.claim: No API operation is documented for the Copilot Studio agent's Allow all and individual MCP-tool selection setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP Allow all individual tools selection API update; Copilot Studio Dataverse botcomponent MCP tool Allow all allowed tools API configuration. Read MCP components page and results for agent tools and MCP configuration; no operation for this setting found.

claims.claim: The printed v2.0 adminconsent URL points to the client app and requests the gateway's /.default scope.
claims.quote: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<customer-tenant-id>/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=<your-client-app-id>&scope=<ATG-app-id>/.default&redirect_uri=<redirect-uri-registered-on-your-app>

claims.claim: The consent operation is on the user's own client app, not the gateway app.
claims.quote: If you prefer a consent URL to the portal, use the v2.0 admin-consent endpoint and point it at your client app, not at the gateway app.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Admin consent on the client app puts McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All into its requested tokens.
claims.quote: Granting admin consent here is what puts McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All into the tokens your client requests. ... If calls are denied, decode the token and check that the scp claim contains McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All.

claims.quote: For MCP servers, registration approval and required Microsoft Entra consent are separate steps. The server becomes available to agent-building surfaces only after consent is granted.

claims.claim: Power Platform connector data policies regulate access to MCP servers and tools in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Access to MCP servers in Copilot Studio relies on Power Platform connectors for connectivity. ... if a data policy regulates Power Platform connectors, it also regulates access to the MCP server and its tools for your agent.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio MCP onboarding process is the same for prebuilt Microsoft connectors and configured MCP connections.
claims.quote: The process is the same, whether you're adding prebuilt Microsoft MCP connectors or an MCP server to which you configured a connection.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot Studio data-policy documentation does not establish coverage for external MCP clients calling this gateway.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Insights MCP server audit log tool calls security roles filter profiles external MCP Power Platform data policies. Read MCP components, gateway and tools-reference pages; connector-based policy scope is stated for Copilot Studio, not external clients.
